app.title: Urban Air Quality Assistant
app.subtitle: Navigate winter smog and urban air pollution with local guidance, indoor air hacks, and low-emission routines.
app.footerNote: Air quality telemetry via Open-Meteo (CC BY 4.0) and WHO 2021 guidelines. Zero tracking; coordinates are never saved.
app.disclaimerShort: Informational guidance only — not medical advice. Consult a doctor for breathing emergencies.

dashboard.smogAlertBody: Fine particles and traffic gases are trapped near street level. Keep windows closed, use an N95 mask outdoors, and shift travel to cleaner hours.
dashboard.inversionNote: High PM2.5 + NO2 pattern indicates stagnant urban inversion conditions.

pollutants.sectionDesc: Measured concentrations in micrograms per cubic meter (µg/m³) compared with World Health Organization 24-hour/8-hour limits.

pm25.name: PM2.5 (Fine Particles)
pm25.shortDesc: Tiny soot and smoke droplets that reach deep into lungs and bloodstream.
pm25.sources: Vehicle exhaust, winter wood/coal smoke, crop burning, dust

pm10.name: PM10 (Coarse Dust)
pm10.shortDesc: Dust and soot particles that irritate nose, throat, and airways.
pm10.sources: Road dust, construction sites, winter haze

no2.name: NO2 (Nitrogen Dioxide)
no2.shortDesc: Traffic gas that inflames airways and triggers asthma flare-ups.
no2.sources: Diesel trucks, cars, power plants, indoor gas stoves

o3.name: O3 (Ground-Level Ozone)
o3.shortDesc: Afternoon sun reacts with exhaust to form lung-irritating smog.

so2.name: SO2 (Sulfur Dioxide)
so2.shortDesc: Sharp gas that tightens airways, especially for people with asthma.
so2.sources: Coal/oil boilers, heavy diesel, industrial plants

co.name: CO (Carbon Monoxide)
co.shortDesc: Colorless gas that reduces oxygen carried in your blood.
co.sources: Idling traffic, poorly vented heaters, solid-fuel stoves

guidance.sectionTitle: Family Health Guidance & Indoor Air Quality Hacks
guidance.profileLegend: Tailor advice to your household and lifestyle

maskAdvice.none_needed: No mask needed today for normal outdoor errands.
maskAdvice.optional_sensitive: Optional well-fitted mask if you feel airway irritation near traffic.
maskAdvice.n95_recommended: Wear a snug N95/FFP2 mask on outdoor trips and busy roads.
maskAdvice.n95_required: Wear a fit-checked N95/FFP2 mask outdoors; cloth/surgical masks do not block PM2.5 smog.

windowsAdvice.open_cross_ventilation: Safe to open windows for fresh cross-ventilation.
windowsAdvice.brief_clean_window: Keep windows closed during rush-hour haze; air out briefly during the cleanest afternoon window.
windowsAdvice.keep_sealed: Keep windows and outer doors closed to block severe smog infiltration.

outdoorAdvice.normal_outdoor: Great air for normal outdoor play, walking, and exercise.
outdoorAdvice.pace_outdoors: Take shorter breaks outdoors and avoid heavy breathing next to busy roads.
outdoorAdvice.shift_indoors: Move vigorous workouts indoors and limit outdoor exposure for sensitive family members.
outdoorAdvice.avoid_outdoors: Stay indoors as much as possible; cancel outdoor sports and protect children and elders.

checklist.smog_check_seal: Seal window gaps with damp towels or weatherstripping during evening smog buildup.
checklist.smog_n95_fit: Pinch the nose bridge on N95/FFP2 masks so polluted air cannot leak around edges.
checklist.sensitive_keep_reliever_ready: Keep prescribed rescue inhalers and emergency contacts within reach.
checklist.ozone_avoid_afternoon_peak: Avoid vigorous outdoor runs during peak afternoon ozone hours.
checklist.hydrate_and_monitor: Drink water regularly and watch local hourly AQI changes before stepping out.

seal_smog_drafts.title: Seal window & door drafts during winter inversion
seal_smog_drafts.desc: Use weatherstripping tape or rolled damp cloths under door gaps between dusk and mid-morning when cold air traps smog outside.

run_hepa_filtration.title: Create a Clean-Air Bedroom Zone with HEPA
run_hepa_filtration.desc: Close bedroom doors and run your HEPA purifier continuously on medium-high so lungs recover for 8+ hours overnight.

build_diy_box_filter.title: Low-cost DIY Box-Fan + MERV-13 Filter Hack
build_diy_box_filter.desc: Tape a MERV-13 furnace filter tightly to the intake side of a standard box fan to cut indoor PM2.5 sharply at a fraction of purifier cost.

wet_mop_dust.title: Wet-mop floors instead of dry sweeping
wet_mop_dust.desc: Dry brooms kick settled PM2.5 and PM10 soot back into breathing height; use a damp microfiber mop or wet cloth.

exhaust_or_induction_cook.title: Ventilate kitchen & use electric appliances
exhaust_or_induction_cook.desc: Gas and biomass flames spike indoor NO2 and fine particles. Always run the exhaust chimney/fan and use an electric kettle or induction burner when possible.

stop_indoor_combustion.title: Zero indoor smoke on high-AQI days
stop_indoor_combustion.desc: Pause incense, scented candles, mosquito coils, and indoor smoking — indoors can trap particles 3× longer than outdoor air.

timed_window_purge.title: Smart 15-minute afternoon cross-ventilation
timed_window_purge.desc: Open opposite windows briefly during the cleanest midday window to flush indoor CO2 without letting morning smog inside.

planner.formulaTitle: How this score is computed (O(n) transparent formula)
planner.formulaDesc: Starts at 100 and subtracts weighted US AQI × breathing-rate intensity × persona sensitivity, plus PM2.5/O3 WHO ratio penalties, plus a daylight/dispersion window adjustment.

shift_to_transit_or_active.title: Switch solo road trips to Metro, bus, or clean-window cycling
shift_to_transit_or_active.desc: Public transit cuts street-level NO2 and PM2.5 emissions per traveler while avoiding stop-and-go exhaust exposure.
shift_to_transit_or_active.whyImpact: Every 10 km shifted from car to metro/bus avoids ~1.3 kg CO2e and ~1.4 g of lung-irritating NOx.

avoid_morning_smog_commute.title: Move errands & commute out of the morning inversion peak
avoid_morning_smog_commute.desc: Winter smog hangs thickest from 6–10 AM before sunlight lifts the inversion lid. Stagger departures or combine afternoon trips.
avoid_morning_smog_commute.whyImpact: Shifting 1 outdoor hour from peak smog to the cleanest afternoon window often halves inhaled PM2.5 dose.

bundle_errands_clean_window.title: Bundle household errands into one midday loop
bundle_errands_clean_window.desc: Combining school, grocery, and pharmacy stops reduces cold-start engine emissions and saves fuel.
bundle_errands_clean_window.whyImpact: Eliminating extra short car starts trims both local NO2 spikes and daily fuel burn.

clean_cooking_switch.title: Shift simmering and boiling to electric induction or kettle
clean_cooking_switch.desc: Replacing open gas or solid-fuel flames for daily tea, rice, and reheating keeps kitchen NO2 and PM2.5 low.
clean_cooking_switch.whyImpact: Prevents indoor PM2.5 surges (~35 µg/m³) that linger inside sealed winter homes.

remote_work_or_carpool.title: Work remotely or carpool on Severe Smog days
remote_work_or_carpool.desc: Coordinate with neighbors and schools to avoid unnecessary vehicles during winter smog emergencies.
remote_work_or_carpool.whyImpact: Removing 1 daily car commute lowers neighborhood tailpipe pollution and shields sensitive lungs.

outdoor_exercise_reschedule.title: Reschedule workouts to the safest daily window
outdoor_exercise_reschedule.desc: Deep breathing during exercise draws up to 3–5× more particles per minute into your lungs.
outdoor_exercise_reschedule.whyImpact: Moving exercise to the planner's top-scoring hour or indoors prevents high-dose particle inhalation.

routines.simulatorTitle: Direct Impact Simulator — See What Your Choices Save
routines.simulatorDesc: Toggle your daily routine swaps to calculate grounded personal exposure reduction and community emissions saved.

toggles.swapCarToCleanTransit: Switch car/two-wheeler trip to metro, bus, or active travel
toggles.shiftActivityToBestWindow: Move outdoor time to today's cleanest window
toggles.wearFittedN95Outdoors: Wear a fitted N95/FFP2 mask during polluted trips
toggles.useCleanCookingAndExhaust: Use electric induction/kettle + exhaust fan indoors
toggles.runIndoorAirFiltration: Run HEPA or DIY box-fan filtration 8 hrs indoors

routines.impactFormulaNote: Calculated from fetched city PM2.5 concentration, active/resting breathing rates (1.8 vs 0.5 m³/h), 92% N95 filtration, and DEFRA/EPA per-km emission factors.
